Exploratory cross-section layout with optional floodplain bends

Source: R/cross_section_layout.R
cross_section_layout.Rd

Estimate separate overbank paths and editable cut lines from reviewed outer inundation footprints. This is a geometry experiment, not a hydraulic model or a replacement legacy feature class.

cross_section_layout(
  flowline,
  channel,
  floodplain,
  spacing_m = 20,
  tangent_distance_m = 20,
  angle_limit_deg = 30,
  centerline_spacing_m = 2,
  smoothing_refinements = 2L,
  region_artifacts = NULL,
  overbank_angle_limit_deg = 30,
  allow_overbank_bends = FALSE
)

Arguments

flowline

One simple LINESTRING, directed downstream to upstream.

channel, floodplain

Hole-filled sf polygon footprints in the same projected CRS as flowline. Channel must be contained in floodplain.

spacing_m

Distance between section centers in metres. Centers begin at half this distance from the downstream endpoint; endpoints are excluded.

tangent_distance_m

Distance along a polygon centerline for measuring its local tangent, in metres; independent of cartographic smoothing.

angle_limit_deg

Historical channel rotation bound, retained for API compatibility. Method v6 uses perpendicular channel cuts without rotation.

centerline_spacing_m

Maximum polygon-boundary vertex spacing in metres.

smoothing_refinements

Number of Chaikin smoothing passes, 0 to 10.

region_artifacts

Optional matching output of cross_section_regions(), reused only when its geometry/settings fingerprint matches these inputs.

overbank_angle_limit_deg

Maximum overbank-normal rotation in degrees, 0 to 60. Straight targets respect this bound; five-degree angular alternatives provide tentative targets before ordered assignment and routing.

allow_overbank_bends

Allow additional floodplain vertices for deconfliction. Defaults to FALSE. Optional polygon-contained routes may have multiple vertices away from the centerline; there is no one-bend cap.

Value

A list with sections (sf lines with at least four XY vertices), paths (separate side estimates), samples (observed/inferred side evidence), failures, conflicts and parameters. Empty or unsupported sections remain explicit failures. candidate_id is a session key, not governed or durable identity. Full-coverage straight/bent alternatives reduce conflicts without shortening legs. Explicit left_bank_vertex and right_bank_vertex identify the channel. Residual conflicts remain explicit. Seq increases upstream. boundary_chains and boundary_anchors retain directed ordering edges and generated bank/planned outer targets in the feature CRS unit.

Details

Contiguous channel crossings containing each center are selected perpendicular to the local centerline tangent. Width minimization and conflict-driven channel rotation are not used. All three polygon centerlines derive from Voronoi skeleton routing and cartographic Chaikin smoothing. An overbank leg uses the component touching its bank vertex. Missing/ambiguous side support retains a flagged bank-only leg. A bank on the outer boundary with no adjacent overbank is separately classified as no_floodplain. If nearest-point matching crosses a channel indentation, the nearest tested segment projection visible through the component supplies the measurement location. The original centerline is unchanged. A one-millimetre numerical polygon margin is used for visibility and connected ray intersections. Bank ranks are checked along directed shared boundaries; outer targets are assigned in Seq order and refined within their ordered neighbor interval before routing. Previously accepted legs and other channel cuts are barriers. A routed endpoint cannot slide along the boundary. These are provisional direction proxies requiring analyst review. All distance parameters are converted to the projected CRS unit. When additional vertices are allowed, GEOS constrained polygon triangulation, igraph paths through triangle portals and visibility shortcuts supply additional routes around neighboring sections. Bends need not be on a centerline. Every route must remain in its component and reach the outer boundary. This optional routing requires GEOS 3.10 or later.
